title: HTTP security headers comprehensive check: CORS misconfiguration, CSP bypass, Clickjacking, HSTS, and information disclosure headers
goal: ZAP passive scan checks some headers but many CORS and CSP issues require active probing. Implement a headers-security runner: (1) CORS misconfiguration (HIGH): send requests with Origin: https://evil.example.com. If Access-Control-Allow-Origin mirrors the attacker origin AND Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true → critical CORS misconfiguration enabling credential theft. Also check: null origin accepted, wildcard + credentials, regex bypass (example.com.evil.com). (2) CSP analysis: parse Content-Security-Policy header and detect: unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval, wildcard (*) in script-src, missing default-src, data: URI in script-src, JSONP endpoint whitelisted. (3) Clickjacking: check for X-Frame-Options: DENY/SAMEORIGIN or frame-ancestors in CSP. If absent AND login/sensitive forms exist → Clickjacking vulnerability. (4) HSTS: check for Strict-Transport-Security header with min-age >= 31536000, includeSubDomains. Absent on HTTPS site → HSTS missing. (5) Information disclosure headers: check for Server version strings (Server: Apache/2.4.49), X-Powered-By (X-Powered-By: PHP/7.2.0), X-AspNet-Version. (6) Open redirect via CORS: check if redirects preserve CORS headers. Passive tier (header analysis) — no approval needed. Active tier for CORS origin reflection test.
scope: WebGoat securitymisconfiguration module + real-world common findings. ZAP checks many of these passively but misses CORS credential reflection (active probe required) and detailed CSP bypass analysis.
generation_reason: CORS misconfiguration with credentials, CSP bypass patterns, and Clickjacking are partially covered by ZAP but miss credential-theft CORS variants — need active probing.
